newsitem.title: FRANCE: French paper says intervention in Zaire contemplated. [CORRECTED 10:45 GMT 03/11]
newsitem.headline: French paper says intervention in Zaire contemplated. [CORRECTED 10:45 GMT 03/11]

text.p: The European Union (EU) is contemplating the opening of militarily-protected "humanitarian corridors" in Zaire to help masses of refugees threatened by fighting in the country, a French newspaper said on Saturday.
The well-informed daily Le Monde wrote from Brussels that such an operation might involve French, Belgian and South African troops.

The French foreign ministry had no immediate reaction to the report, but Italy's foreign ministry said earlier that "suitable measures of protection" were needed so the United Nations could aid refugees in eastern Zaire.
Most aid agencies have pulled out of chaotic east Zaire, where they were helping about a million Rwandan Hutu refugees.

Fighting between the Zairean army and ethnic Tutsi rebels backed by the Tutsi-led Rwandan army has resulted in the rebels seizing several towns in a 250-km (160-mile) stretch of eastern Zaire. (Corrects to delete reference to Tutsi-led Rwandan army capturing several Zairean towns. The army has only been reported present in Goma.)

Le Monde wrote that France told its partners it would not intervene militarily unless it was mandated to do so, preferably by the Organisation of African Unity which is due to meet imminently in Nairobi, Kenya.

France sent troops to halt civil strife in Rwanda in 1994 and is still smarting under accusations that its quasi-unilateral intervention was mostly aimed at advancing French policy objectives in the region.
A foreign ministry statement on Saturday made no mention of military intervention but said humanitarian aid could only be brought to the area if fighting there ceased.
Paris said it fully backed U.N. and EU initiatives and favoured a regional conference which has so far received no support from the countries involved.

The Italian foreign ministry earlier said: "In light of the worsening situation of the refugees in the region of Kivu, on the border between Rwanda and Zaire, Italy asks the United Nations to urgently organise an intervention of humanitarian aid, with the suitable measures of protection, to which Italy, also within the European Union, is ready to give its support."
